# TurnOver 2.0, build 17 (in progress)
TurnOver is now built in Swift 6 language mode with the main-actor default: the compiler checks every thread boundary (speech, the key tap, the background page walks), which is why the version number moves to 2.0. Nothing changes in how it is used.
### Keys that moved: please read this first
TurnOver now has three sets of keys. In the Mac style, VoiceOver's keys do exactly what they do in VoiceOver. In the Windows style, NVDA's keys do exactly what they do in NVDA. And TurnOver's own commands sit behind one key, the same in both styles, that works even in an app VoiceOver reads: **Command Control Comma, then a letter** (Oliver).
Why one key: Apple's own apps use nearly every Command Control letter (we read the menus of Finder, Safari, Mail, Terminal, Preview, Xcode and more: Command Control N, T and R alone are taken by five or six of them), and TurnOver shouldn't take shortcuts away from the apps you use. JAWS users will know this as a layered key. **Tell us what you think of it**: Send feedback, or reply on AppleVis.
- **Command Control Comma, then N: the TurnOver menu.** In the Mac style, VO-N is now VoiceOver's: the notifications you've heard lately. In the Windows style, Caps Lock N still opens the menu, as NVDA's does. - **Command Control Comma, then T: hand the app in front back to VoiceOver** (or back to TurnOver), and remember it. The TurnOver menu, Hand over or quit, does it too. VO-V is now VoiceOver's verbosity list, and Caps Lock V NVDA's screen layout. Nothing is lost: the way back to VoiceOver is always there. - **Command Control Period: start or quit TurnOver**, a single press, from anywhere (it was Command Control T). - The other letters: **S** settings, **K** keyboard style, **J** "that was wrong", **Slash** the shortcuts here, **P** the plugin maker, **C** copy the last thing said, **H** the guide, **I** describe a picture, **R** screen recognition. Any other key says the letters; Escape or three seconds cancels. - In the Mac style, VoiceOver's own keys for these work too: VO-H twice the commands, VO-Slash a custom label (the plugin maker), VO-Shift-Slash the guide, VO-F8 settings, VO-Shift-C copy the last phrase, VO-Shift-L describe. - **The latest messages in Messages and WhatsApp, and the parts of a window in apps with panes, are Command Control 1 to 9** (those apps' own keys, where TurnOver reads them). In the Mac style, VO-1 to VO-0 are now VoiceOver's hot spots; in the Windows style, Caps Lock 1 to 5 are NVDA's again (input help, typed characters and words, command keys, dynamic content). - Windows style, as NVDA: Control stops speech and Shift pauses it; Caps Lock Up and Down Arrow move the review cursor by line (Caps Lock L reads the line, Caps Lock A says all); Caps Lock Shift Z is sleep mode for the app in front. Mac style, as VoiceOver: Control pauses and carries on.
### New to try
- **Keys have moved.** TurnOver's own commands are Command Control Comma, then a letter, in both styles and any app: N the menu, T hand the app to VoiceOver or back, S settings, K keyboard style, J that was wrong, Slash the shortcuts here, H the guide, I describe a picture, C copy what was said, R screen recognition, P the plugin maker. Command Control Period starts or quits TurnOver. In the Mac style VoiceOver's keys, and in the Windows style NVDA's, do exactly what they do there. - **The Mac style is VoiceOver's.** 178 of the 189 commands in Apple's VoiceOver guide behave as in VoiceOver, among them the notifications list (VO-N), verbosity (VO-V), hot spots (VO-Shift with a digit to set, VO with a digit to go), the speech settings (VO-Command with the arrows), the help menu (VO-H), the Find commands (VO-Shift-F), style changes and same-level headings (VO-Command-C, VO-Command-M), tables (VO-R, VO-C, VO-Shift-T), paragraphs and sentences, and moving and resizing windows. - **The Windows style is NVDA's.** 114 of the 130 commands in NVDA's reference: the review cursor, table navigation (Control with Command and the arrows on a Mac keyboard), the clipboard (Caps Lock C), repeat (Caps Lock X), sleep mode (Caps Lock Shift Z), screen layout (Caps Lock V), the synth settings ring, and Control to stop speech and Shift to pause it. - **The keypad.** Mac style: VoiceOver's NumPad Commander, with VoiceOver's own keys; VO-Clear turns it on. Windows style: NVDA's desktop layout (7 8 9 lines, 4 5 6 words, 1 2 3 characters, keypad 0 held as the NVDA key); Clear switches between commands and typing numbers. - **Audio ducking.** Other apps' sound is lowered while TurnOver speaks: Settings, Speech, or Caps Lock Shift D in the Windows style. Off to start with. The first time, macOS asks to let TurnOver record system audio; nothing is kept. - **Plugins.** Label an unnamed button, give an item a key, have it read when it changes, or keep it quiet: VO-Slash, or Command Control Comma then P. A careful first step: plugins can do more in coming builds, each asking for what it needs. - **Google Docs, Sheets and Slides.** TurnOver reads Google's own announcements as you move and type, as NVDA does. Google's screen reader support must be on: Command Option Z in a document; TurnOver tells you if it's off. - **System prompts.** Prompts that appear behind your app ("would like to use your location") are read, and Tab and Space work in them. - **The TurnOver menu is tidier.** This app first, then Settings, Apps, Keys, What to test, Send feedback, Tools, About and updates, Hand over or quit. - **Microsoft Excel.** Cells are read as you move, content then address ("Monday, A2"); selecting says the range. - **Right Option T.** It says the time, and twice quickly the date. - **Your own keys.** TurnOver menu, Keys: give any key to a command, or take one away. - **Speech.** Capitals can be said at a higher pitch, and speech can play on a chosen device: Settings, Speech. - **Messages, Finder and Safari.** In Messages, Command T opens the Tapback reactions as a list. Finder reads desktop and icon view items with their kind. Safari says the new tab's title as you switch tabs.
### What to test
- The layer key: Command Control Comma, then N, S, K, J; and in an app VoiceOver reads (Calculator, say). - Your usual work in your usual style: anything a key did before that it no longer does, tell us. - Google Docs or Sheets, with Google's screen reader support on: moving, typing, the menus. - The keypad, if you use one, in your style. - A plugin: label an unnamed button in an app you use, then undo it. - Ducking, with music playing.
### Fixed
- Word: TurnOver no longer quits when you come back into a table you had just left (Mohammad).
- Typing straight after Backspace in Claude's prompt (and other web text boxes) came late: each Backspace waited for the box to report its caret. TurnOver now lets the next key through at once, as NVDA does (Oliver). - System prompts that appear behind the app you're in ("would like access to record your system audio", "would like to use your current location") are now said, as VoiceOver says them, and get the keyboard. In these protected prompts Tab and Space go straight to macOS, and if macOS refuses a VO-Space press TurnOver puts the focus back on your choice and asks for Space (Oliver). - In a dialog, Tab and VO-Space now agree: VO-Space presses the choice Tab reached (Oliver). - VO-Command-C (next style change) gives up after a third of a second rather than holding TurnOver up in a long note. - The keypad stops speech as other keys do, and leaves sleeping apps and "pass next key" alone. - Sleep mode no longer traps TurnOver's own menu over a sleeping app. - "That was wrong" only marks the moment; pressing it twice no longer sends a report by itself. - The clipboard (NVDA+C), link addresses and notifications are spoken but no longer written into the log or reports, which could carry a copied password or a two-factor code. - The shortcuts list shows only keys that really do what it says in the current style.
- TurnOver Shift T no longer says the time: it was a tester's preference, not NVDA's or VoiceOver's (VO-Shift-T is a table's row and column now, in the Mac style). - Keyboard help names the modifier keys as you press them: command, shift, option, control (left or right), function, and caps lock, the TurnOver key. Control no longer pauses speech while keyboard help is on (Oliver). - Windows style: Control Right goes to the start of the next word and reads it, as NVDA does; it read the text passed over (JC). - Opening TurnOver from Finder or Spotlight no longer leaves you on TurnOver itself ("TurnOver has no windows"): it steps back to the app you were in (Chelsea). - Feedback reports are kept in TurnOver's own folder, the newest ten, not on the Desktop (a synced Desktop sent them all to the cloud); a copy goes on the Desktop only when no mail app opens (Chelsea). - The Voice menu lists voices for the languages set on your Mac, so a Spanish speaker can choose a Spanish voice for TurnOver itself (Agustín). - The function keys are never touched (build 16 could switch off "Use F1, F2 as standard function keys"; turn it back on once in System Settings, Keyboard) (Urh). - Reminders: Tab in a new reminder announced the window between the title and the notes. Tab out of the sidebar had been judged "ignored" too quickly, and TurnOver then took Tab over in text fields too. Text fields now always get the app's own Tab, and TurnOver waits a little longer before deciding an app ignores it (Oliver). - Right and Left on a sidebar item answer at once ("expanded", "collapsed"), with the edge sound where there is nothing to open; they used to wait and say nothing. - Text is never announced as "text": iPhone apps on the Mac (Books, Audible) said "Home, text, selected". - Icon buttons with only a tooltip are named by it, as VoiceOver does (Cyberduck's Back, Forward, Browser, Bookmarks and History were just "button"). - Web pages inside apps (Bambu Studio's release notes): list numbers say "1", not "unknown, 1"; a heading is one stop, not read twice; icon-font symbols are no longer read as names. - After waking or unlocking the Mac, TurnOver could hear none of your keys for several seconds (the lock screen's password field keeps the Mac's secure input on for a moment). VoiceOver now keeps the Mac until that is over, then TurnOver takes back the app in front (Oliver). - Chrome and Edge: tables are read once, by rows (they were read by rows, then by columns, then the header again); each item of a list is its own line (Google Drive's files ran together); toggle buttons say "toggle button, pressed", not "check box"; dialogs, menu bars and tool bars are named as you enter them. - Excel opened fresh: its cells are read from the first arrow (it said nothing until Excel had been open a while). - Switching to an app whose first focus has no name (Excel) no longer leaves the last app's text box in charge: its arrows were answered silently. - Preview: pages are read as "page", not "unknown, unavailable"; tool groups are "grouping"; lists and other containers are no longer said to be "unavailable". - A dot between words (Byword's "Markdown • 61 words") is read as a pause, not "bullet". A value that repeats the name is said once (Excel's headings). Review no longer stops on a table's untitled columns (Ulysses). - Reminders: Tab between a reminder's title and its notes said the window and the list before each field. The window's passing focus is now held a quarter of a second and said only if nothing else takes the focus (Oliver). - Tabs say which one is showing ("Input, tab, selected, 2 of 2"). On the Mac the arrows move between tabs without switching, and Space switches; TurnOver did not say which was selected (Oliver, System Settings' Sound). - Switches say "switch, on" or "switch, off", as VoiceOver does, not "toggle button, pressed". - A control reported twice (SwiftUI apps such as System Settings hand over two references for one) is read once. - Review reads a row once: no more the row, then its cell, then each text in it (Reminders, Contacts, System Settings; the duplicates heard in the Windows style). Faster in long lists (Contacts). - Focus on a scroll area itself says what it holds ("…, scroll area"), where it was silent (Shortcuts' editor). - Safari: Enter or Space on a button you have tabbed to (a cookie banner's "Accept all cookies") pressed the link before it, or went to the group around it. They now go to the button the keyboard is on (Oliver). - Web pages: misspelled words in fields now say "spelling error", and inside a line, not only at its start (Lorien). - Live regions inside other live regions are said once, not twice (Mert, The Playroom). - Finder: Command Down with nothing selected (after Command Up to the top) says so, rather than nothing (Stuart). - WhatsApp with no chat open: the arrows go straight into the conversations (it said nothing until Tab), the arrows and Return work the sections when WhatsApp's own focus is on one, and Escape no longer drops the cursor (Oliver, 10 Oct 2026). - Function keys: TurnOver no longer changes them at all. They behave as set in System Settings, Keyboard ("Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys"). Earlier builds switched them with the reader and put them back as media keys every time (Mert). - TurnOver T reads the window's title as it is now; after a Safari tab switch it said the old one (Mert). - Space in Podcasts, Music and other lists now plays and pauses, and in Finder opens Quick Look: TurnOver only takes Space when the selected row has a check box to tick (Oliver, 10 Oct 2026).
- Speech follows the Mac's output device: headphones or speakers chosen after TurnOver started now get its voice (AirPods Max left TurnOver on the speakers, 9 Oct 2026). Confirmed by Oliver switching back and forth.

# TurnOver 1.0, build 16
### New to try
- A slider or other control read as its value changes now reads the new value, not the one it had when it took the focus; a slider from 0 to 1 is said as a percentage. - Mac style: VO M twice, the status menus, now includes TurnOver's own item at the end. - Mac style: on a web page, typing while the reading position is on a text field goes into that field, as it does once VoiceOver's cursor lands on one; the field takes the focus and focus mode starts. In the Windows style letters stay quick-nav keys until Enter or Tab goes into the field, as in NVDA. - Tab on a web page no longer announces the group a control sits in ("Description of App, grouping" on AppleVis). - TurnOver Shift T reads the time, twice for the date, for Macs without an Insert key or the function keys (JC). - A short start-up tone when TurnOver starts while VoiceOver has the Mac, so with Open at login you know it is there (Daniel). - Force quit, spoken. Command Option Escape (and Control Shift Escape in the Windows style) lists the running applications; choose one, then confirm to force quit it or ask it to quit normally. The Mac's own Force Quit window is silent with VoiceOver off. Also in the TurnOver menu as "Force quit an application". - Automatic language switching now works in any app, not only where the text is marked with its language: a line in another script (Arabic under an English voice, or the other way round) is read with that language's voice in TextEdit, Pages or anywhere else, and so is a single character when you move by character (reported by a tester). - The formatting key (VO T; TurnOver F in the Windows style) reports the first selected character when text is selected, and says "selected" first. Pressed twice, it gives the detail: colour, background colour, superscript or subscript, and alignment where the application reports it (requested by a tester). - Word tables: TurnOver Up and Down move by row and Left and Right by column from wherever the caret is, and the table's size is said once. A new switch in Preferences, Document formatting, "Table row and column headers" (requested by a tester). - Under the bonnet: Messages and WhatsApp are now described by small recipe files rather than code (the first step towards adding apps without a build, and towards plugins). You can put your own recipe for another chat app in ~/Library/Application Support/TurnOver/recipes; a file that won't load is named in the log. - Windows style: a review step (TurnOver and the arrows) onto a control took the keyboard focus with it, as VoiceOver's cursor does, so after reviewing TextEdit's toolbar the arrows had left the text. NVDA's review cursor never moves the focus, so it no longer does in the Windows style; a setting in Preferences, Keyboard ("Keyboard focus follows the cursor") chooses: by style, on, or off. - Safari: H on a heading long enough to wrap over two lines read only its first line, and the next H landed on its second line as if it were another heading (reported by Oliver). Quick navigation now reads the whole heading and skips to the next one. - Finder: Command Up and Command Down made TurnOver hand over to VoiceOver for a few seconds (macOS reported TurnOver's own process in front for a moment), which felt like a crash. TurnOver no longer hands over on account of its own process unless one of its own windows is showing (reported by a tester). - Mac style: VO M no longer has the focused item spoken over "Apple menu"; and after closing a menu with Escape, the focused item is read once, not three times (reported by a tester). - Under the bonnet, from this week's code review: TurnOver's keys are decided on its main thread now, so an application that stops answering can no longer make macOS switch TurnOver's keyboard off (a TurnOver chord's letter then landed in the document). Nothing changes in how the keys work; it should feel the same or quicker. - The App Store's End key (reading to the end of a long page) and Word's headings list (VO U) no longer hold TurnOver up while they wait for the application: "please wait" is said if they take long, and speech carries on meanwhile.
### Fixed - Mac style: after reading from a field with the VO keys (VO Command Shift H from Claude's prompt), the first letter typed was taken as a quick-navigation key and only the later ones went into the field. A typed key now goes straight back to the field (reported by Oliver). - If a chosen voice went silent, the guide now says how to get speech back: Command Control T for VoiceOver, then one line in Terminal (under "If something goes wrong"). - VO Right and VO Left along a big window (Music's grid, System Settings) asked the application thousands of questions a key; the answer is kept for a moment while you step along the same group. - The log's "ms after the last key" figure was nonsense before the first key. - TurnOver now has automated tests that run on every build, and a way of recording a window so an app can be tested without it running (TESTING.md). - Quitting TurnOver from outside (a kill, an installer) now tidies up as a quit from the menu does: the top row back to the media keys, the curtain off. - A BAUM display unplugged while TurnOver was using it could crash it later; fixed. - Switching TurnOver off and on again at once could leave its keyboard layer half torn down; each start now has a layer of its own. - A hand-over to VoiceOver that needed a second try could be read as you pinning the app to VoiceOver by hand; fixed. - The code that decides which focus reports to follow is now nineteen named rules, one per special case, with tests; it should behave exactly as before, so please report any app where the focus seems to go astray.

# TurnOver 1.0, build 15
### New to try - Messages and WhatsApp (previews, off until you turn them on in the TurnOver menu, Applications). Your keyboard stays in the message box. Tab takes you to the messages, starting on the newest, and Shift Tab to the conversations. There, Up and Down move, Home and End go to the first and last, Return opens a conversation, and the shortcut menu (VO Shift M, or the right Option key in the Windows style) lists the message's own actions: reply, tapback, copy and so on. Escape goes back to the message box. TurnOver 1 to 9 read the latest messages from anywhere in the window, 1 the newest. New messages in the open conversation are read as they arrive. With no conversation open (WhatsApp), Tab goes straight to the conversations. In WhatsApp, the shortcut menu on a message opens WhatsApp's own menu for it (reply, react, forward and more), and Tab goes on from the chats to WhatsApp's bar of sections (Chats, Updates, Communities, Calls, Archived, Starred): Return shows that section's chats. The chats are found in whichever section is showing.
- Spelling errors anywhere: TurnOver E and TurnOver Shift E (VO Command E and VO Command Shift E in the Mac style) go to the next and previous misspelled word in any text, not just Word: TextEdit, Mail's message body, and text boxes on web pages, such as AppleVis's comment box. - Braille: the display now shows what you're on, not what TurnOver says. Try arrowing through Mail's list, the TurnOver menu, a menu-bar menu, WhatsApp's chats and Music's shelves, and reading back through Terminal; try typing on the display in Claude's prompt or a chat box. - Document formatting has a new setting, "Heading, link and button: say them": after the words, as VoiceOver ("AppleVis, heading level 1"), or before them, as NVDA. Out of the box it follows the keyboard style: after in the Mac style, before in the Windows style (requested by a tester). - Notifications from other apps (a new message, a calendar alert) are read as they appear, as VoiceOver and NVDA do. Presentation has a switch for it (requested by a tester). - Browse mode has NVDA's "screen layout" setting: links flow with the text as on screen, or each goes on a line of its own (requested by a tester). - Browse mode has NVDA's automatic focus mode setting: a field taking the focus switches to focus mode by itself, or only when you ask (requested by a tester). - The menu bar, as each style has it. Mac style: VO M lands on the Apple menu's title, Left and Right go along the bar, Down opens the menu and Escape leaves, as VoiceOver. Windows style: Command on its own opens the Apple menu, and Up and Down move through it as a list, as NVDA. Both start at the Apple menu, as the Mac does. The status menus too: VO M twice in the Mac style lands on them, Left and Right move along, Down opens one; Option B in the Windows style lists them.
### Fixed - A review of the whole code base (8 Oct 2026) fixed: feedback reports no longer include what the braille display showed, notification banners, page titles or speech in other languages; speech comes back by itself when headphones or AirPods connect (the audio engine stopped and stayed stopped); say all says "end of document" after blank lines and the next arrow no longer resumes it; the braille cursor shows at the end of a line; a held dot 7 stops deleting if the display drops; settings are saved atomically and a settings file that won't read is kept beside the new one, not thrown away; a new setting can no longer wipe the list of apps TurnOver leads in; VoiceOver is started by opening VoiceOver.app if its shortcut doesn't bring it back; the tester-key-withdrawn alert is read; switching into focus mode by itself always says so; a page that gets shorter no longer leaves Left and Right stuck; five crashes on odd accessibility answers (a window closing mid-read, a stale item index in Music, a shrinking Finder sidebar, position values that aren't positions, Word's table cells). - Mail: Return in the search field now says how many results there are and goes to them (nothing was said, and Tab went to the toolbar). Command Option F no longer reads the whole message the focus passes through on its way to the search field. - Music: Return on a song in the library says "playing"; VO Shift N in the library says what's playing, not the table's hint. - Terminal, Mac style: VO Up and VO Down read back through the output, as VoiceOver reads the screen. - Mac style: leaving the menu bar with Escape or VO M says where you are. - Mail: Command Shift D says "sent" once the message has gone (reported by a tester). - Status menus: items that give no name (Control Center's on macOS 26) are named from their identifiers instead of all being "Control Center" (reported by a tester). In the Mac style, VO M twice lands on the status menus and Left and Right move along them, as VoiceOver. - Menus: moving between menu-bar menus with Left and Right no longer reads the app's focus ("message body") in the gap between one menu closing and the next opening (reported by a tester). - Mail's shortcut menu: letters go to its search box, which filters the menu; TurnOver now says what you've typed, and "no matches" when nothing is left, instead of going quiet. - Mail: VO arrows in a big message list slowed down with every key until VoiceOver took over. They now answer straight away, however many messages there are (reported by a tester). - Next and previous spelling error (TurnOver E, TurnOver Shift E, VO Command E) work in any text: TextEdit, Mail's message body and web pages' text boxes (AppleVis's comment box), not just Word (reported by a tester). - A voice that doesn't speak in TurnOver no longer leaves it silent: TurnOver goes back to a voice that works and tells you (reported by a tester). - Mail: a message opened in its own window could leave you stuck on its header, a blank field where the arrows read nothing. Reading now starts in the message. - The cursor no longer says a heading's name twice ("Discover, heading, Discover" in the App Store). - Terminal: new output wasn't read at all, and Return said "new line". A macOS update changed how Terminal describes itself; TurnOver recognises it again. - Podcasts: search results are read properly (no more just "Explicit"), Return opens a show, and a show's page no longer reads the search results behind it. Follow, Play and the other header buttons are each their own item. - Music, Podcasts and TV: Tab now reaches a fourth area, the tool bar, with Back, Share, More and Search. More opens the menu with Unfollow, Add to Library, Delete from Library and the rest. - Music, Podcasts and TV: Space says what it did (playing, paused, stopped), and corrects itself if the app changes its mind. Live radio's Stop and a played episode's Replay are understood. If something doesn't start (it may need a subscription or a download), TurnOver says so instead of "playing". - Music, Podcasts and TV: searching reads the results and puts you on them. "Middle dot" and "bullet" are no longer read in titles. Status lines such as "Refreshing content" and "Loading…" aren't items any more. - Music, Podcasts, TV and the App Store: opened from the Dock or Spotlight (not switched to), they now read the page as soon as it appears, instead of just the app's name. - Alerts in Music and the App Store ("Delete these songs?") say each button as you Tab. - WhatsApp: Tab in the search field goes to the results (chats, contacts and messages that match), even with a chat open. - WhatsApp: Media is in the sections; Calls lists your calls; Settings works with Tab, the arrows and Caps Lock arrows, each page says its title, and Escape goes back a page or closes Settings (WhatsApp ignores Escape and Command W there). - WhatsApp: coming back with Command Tab says where you are; opening a chat says the message box once, not twice; your own message isn't read again when it changes from sent to delivered to read. - Messages: Return in the message box says "sent", not "new line". - Mac style: VO Right and VO Left read a window column by column (WhatsApp's sidebar, chats and chat no longer interleave), and start with the window's close, minimise and full screen buttons, as VoiceOver does. Text that keeps its words in a description (WhatsApp's sidebar) is no longer skipped, and nested headings say their name. - VO Space on something that opens and closes (WhatsApp's More) says "expanded" or "collapsed". - Something focused inside a container of the same name (WhatsApp's Settings) is said once. - Word: closing Find with Escape reads what was found; Command Tab back to Word reads the line you're on; dialogs and the Save sheet no longer say "document" between their fields; inserting a table no longer says "out of table". - Word, Mac style: VO Up and VO Down move by rows in a table, as VO Left and VO Right move by cells. In the page, VO Left and VO Right move by character, as VoiceOver, instead of jumping to the sidebar. - Windows style: Caps Lock F reports the formatting, as NVDA+F. Find is Caps Lock Control F, with Caps Lock F3 and Shift F3 for the next and previous match. - Formatting says the language by name ("English (United Kingdom)"), not its code. - Return on a button in an alert sheet presses that button, not the alert's default: in Claude's "Claude is still working" alert, Return on "Quit anyway" pressed Cancel. - Word: choosing a heading in the rotor (VO U) goes to it and reads it, instead of landing in the sidebar. - Lists whose rows hold their name as a heading (System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation) read the name, not just "collapsed". - Braille: the display shows what you're on, not what TurnOver says. "New line", window names, "selected …" and "end of document" no longer cover the line for seconds; Mail's list, the TurnOver menu, WhatsApp's and Messages' chats and messages, and the shelves of Music, Podcasts, TV and the App Store all show on the display and stay there. Roles and states use NVDA's short forms (btn, chk, lnk, h2). A message gives way as soon as you move. - Braille in Word: the line you're on shows as you type and move (it showed only "doc"). - Braille: menu items show on the display as you arrow through a menu (a "Mail menu" message was hiding them), and the menu bar's title no longer comes back after the menu closes. Terminal's review lines show on the display as you read back. - Word: Command B, I and U say "bold on", "italic off" and so on once, not twice. - Braille typing on a web page in browse mode, with the keyboard in a text field (after reading Claude's reply with VO Command H), switches to focus mode in the field, so the display shows what you type. - Braille typing: typing fast no longer jumps the focus to the Dock. A space that lands just after a letter, while you're typing, types the letter and a space instead of running a command ("a" with space was "previous item"). Space with dots 3 4 says where you are, as in VoiceOver. Input help says plainly when a chord isn't a command. - Braille typing: a word whose last cell was pressed together with space (the word "the" with space a moment early) is typed, not lost. Dot 7 says what it deleted. Return or dot 8 that sends a message (Claude, chat boxes) no longer says "new line".
